Hey Product Hunt 👋 [...] How it works

 Open your local site in your browser and click an element. Shift-click to select more than one.
 Describe the change: “Match this button’s height to the one beside it.”
 Send it to Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode and follow the agent’s activity beside the page.
 Review the proposed diff in your browser. Approve or reject it in review mode, or enable auto-apply when you want it.

Built for the tools you already use  
PulseDev works with your own browser, local project and installed coding agent. Add the widget with a script tag, or use the Vite plugin for source mapping where supported. Your agent’s usual usage limits and provider charges still apply. [...] It’s for the UI work that adds up: adjusting spacing, matching styles between elements, changing copy, and polishing the details before you ship.

Free for one project on macOS. Pro unlocks unlimited projects. Subscribe before November 3, 2026 for $12/month and keep that rate. New subscriptions are $18/month from November 3. No promo code needed.

I’d love to hear about your workflow  
- Think about the last UI change you asked a coding agent to make. What was harder: explaining which element you meant, or getting the change right?  
- How do you share UI context today—screenshots, selectors, file paths, or descriptions?  
- What would you need to see before trusting the proposed change?  
- After trying PulseDev, where did you still have to explain yourself?
